estrutura.personaBrief: Akbar built a centralized empire with subahs run by appointed governors and mansabdars removable by the emperor, uniform revenue and coinage; local autonomy existed only as tributary arrangements under imperial sovereignty.

representacao.personaBrief: An absolute monarch with no elections, who claimed final arbiter authority in religion (Mahzar) and ruled through appointed, merit-ranked officials answerable only to him.

poder.personaBrief: His state was coercive and watchful (spy network, imperial kotwals, severe punishments, sack of Chittor) yet tolerated bhang/opium use and sought to curb coercive sati; liberty was subordinate to imperial order.

imigracao.personaBrief: Akbar ran a cosmopolitan Persianate court welcoming Persians, Central Asians, Hindus, Jains, Parsis and Jesuits, with sulh-i-kul as universal tolerance and no demand of cultural conversion.

diplomacia.personaBrief: A lifelong conqueror who maintained a large standing army and artillery, waged expansion in Rajputana, Gujarat, Bengal and Kashmir, and used diplomacy mainly to extract submission.

intervencao.personaBrief: Akbar asserted imperial dominance over neighbors, absorbing or subordinating them by force or marriage alliance, and treated no external authority as binding on him.

economia.personaBrief: The crown claimed vast land revenue, ran imperial workshops (karkhanas), mints and a salaried-assignment nobility, while private merchants and artisans flourished under state regulation.

controle.personaBrief: Todar Mal's zabt system fixed assessments, standardized coinage and weights, set official prices and wages, and the emperor directed the economy centrally through the mansabdari apparatus.

comercio.personaBrief: He promoted trade, safe roads, a single currency and welcomed foreign merchants and Portuguese traders, but under imperial control and for revenue and prestige.

religiao.personaBrief: A devout and mystical Muslim-born ruler who debated all faiths at the Ibadat Khana and created the Din-i Ilahi; religion was central to rule, though inclusive, never secular.

moral.personaBrief: A patriarchal 16th-century monarch with a harem who nonetheless curbed forced sati and promoted meat abstention; socially traditional with reformist touches, favoring gradual change.

tecnologia.personaBrief: A curious patron of rational inquiry, artillery, architecture and new cities like Fatehpur Sikri, favoring practical progress though from a pre-industrial world.
